title: How a submarine dives and surfaces

parts.label: Hull
parts.brief: A long, smooth, cigar-shaped body with a rounded nose at the front and a gently tapering tail. It is painted dark grey-black with faint rows of rivets and thin weld seams running around it. This strong steel shell keeps the deep sea's huge pressure out.

parts.label: Sail (tower)
parts.brief: A tall, narrow fin-shaped tower standing on top of the hull, rounded at the front and flat on the sides. It is dark grey with a few small round windows near the top and a thin hand rail around the top edge. It holds the periscope and masts.

parts.label: Periscope
parts.brief: A thin silver metal tube rising straight up from the top of the sail. At the top is a small boxy head with a glass lens window facing forward. It lets the crew peek above the waves while the submarine stays hidden.

parts.label: Ballast tanks
parts.brief: A big rounded tank shaped like a fat capsule, made of steel and painted orange-red so it stands out inside the hull. It has small flood holes along its bottom where seawater can rush in, and a pipe connection on top. There is one near the front and one near the back.

parts.label: Vent valves
parts.brief: A small round valve on top of the hull with a short pipe stub and a little hinged flap lid, in shiny brass. When it opens, air escapes out of the ballast tank below it. There is one above each ballast tank.

parts.label: Compressed air tanks
parts.brief: A bundle of long, thin steel bottles lying side by side, like big scuba tanks, painted light blue with silver end caps. Thin pipes run from their necks toward the ballast tanks. They hold air squeezed very tightly.

parts.label: Dive planes
parts.brief: A short, flat fin sticking straight out from each side of the hull near the tail, like a small stubby wing. It is dark grey with a thin hinge line so it can tilt up or down. Tilting them points the submarine's nose up or down as it moves.

parts.label: Propeller
parts.brief: A large bronze propeller at the very back of the hull, with seven curved blades around a rounded centre hub. The blades are wide and swept like a fan. It spins to push the submarine forward through the water.

steps.say: This is a submarine! It is a ship that can float on top of the sea, then sink down deep under the waves, and come back up again. Let's find out how it does that trick.
First, the hull. It is a super strong steel shell. Deep down, the water presses in really hard, like an elephant sitting on every window, so the hull has to be tough.
Let's look inside! These orange tanks are ballast tanks. When they are full of air, the submarine floats, like a beach ball bobbing on a pool.
To dive, the crew opens the vent valves on top. The air rushes out, and seawater pours in through holes at the bottom. Now the submarine is heavier, so down it goes!
To come back up, the vents close and air squeezed into these tanks gets blown into the ballast tanks. It pushes the water out, like blowing water out of a straw. Lighter again, so up it floats!
The propeller spins to push the submarine forward. The dive planes at the back tilt like little wings to point its nose up or down, and the periscope peeks above the waves.
Now watch all the parts slide back together! Let air out to sink, blow air in to rise. That's how a submarine dives and surfaces.

recap: A submarine sinks by filling its ballast tanks with water and rises by blowing that water out with air.
question: What would you want to see if you could ride a submarine down to the bottom of the sea?
